# PR #3081: Patch: a job ran over 7 minutes

Closes #3058

## What changed

`rust (test tools, wasm)` ran 7m30s, and most of its time went to three groups of tests in the `jackioh` bin that play whole AI games at the full `AI_GATE_BUDGET`. Those tests prove how a game is dealt, seated, replayed or filed, not how well the AI plays it. They now play at a smaller budget, and every assertion is unchanged.

- **`crates/tools/src/arena.rs`**: a new `#[cfg(test)] pub(crate) const TEST_BUDGET` of 150 nodes, 40 lethal nodes and 1 determinization, the rest as `AI_GATE_BUDGET`. `r850000_one_ai_on_both_seats_splits_every_deal` and `r747000_a_mid_skill_game_reproduces_and_replays` set `self_budget` to it.
- **`crates/tools/src/selfplay.rs`**: `play_chunks` is now a wrapper over a new `play_chunks_at(…, budget, …)`, and the old body moved there. `play_chunks` passes `AI_GATE_BUDGET`, so `run` and every production path behave as before. The test-only `play` wraps a new test-only `play_at`, which takes a budget.
- **`crates/tools/src/selfplay_records.rs`**: the tests' `exported()` plays the two games once, at `TEST_BUDGET`, and both tests share them through a `OnceLock`. Game n doesn't depend on how many games follow it, so `exported(1)` returns the same game as before.

No test was added, deleted or ignored. No `allow`, no new ruling and no spec change. The changed tests keep their R-ids and names.

## A person must edit `.github/workflows/ci.yml`

The bot can't touch `.github/`. These changes alone bring the job to about 5m10 by my estimate. That is under the 7-minute alert but not reliably under the 5-minute target. In the `rust-test` matrix, replace the last entry (`group: tools, wasm`) with these three:

```yaml
          - group: tools arena
            scope: tools_wasm
            cache: tools-wasm
            test: '-p jackioh-tools --bin jackioh --config profile.test.package.jackioh-luau.opt-level=0 -- arena:: selfplay_records::'
          - group: tools gate
            scope: tools_wasm
            cache: tools-wasm
            test: '-p jackioh-tools --bin jackioh --config profile.test.package.jackioh-luau.opt-level=0 -- gate::tests::'
          - group: tools, wasm
            scope: tools_wasm
            cache: tools-wasm
            test: '--workspace --exclude jackioh-engine --exclude jackioh-cards --exclude jackioh-server --exclude jackioh-ai --exclude jackioh-luau --config profile.test.package.jackioh-luau.opt-level=0 --config profile.test.package.jackioh-engine.opt-level=1 --config profile.test.package.jackioh-cards.opt-level=0 -- --skip fuzz:: --skip selfplay:: --skip positions:: --skip arena:: --skip selfplay_records:: --skip gate::tests::'
```

- **`gate::tests::`, not `gate::`**: the shorter filter also matches 10 `fuzz::tests::fuzz_m4_gate::` tests that `tools fuzz` already runs.
- **Opt-levels**: the catch-all builds the engine at opt-level 1 and the cards at 0, as `engine rules` does. The two AI-game groups keep opt-level 2, because at engine 1 and cards 0 their tests took 86 s instead of 51 s. The three groups can share the `tools-wasm` cache key, because only workspace crates differ.
- **Same edit**: update the comment above the tools groups (`in three groups by test name… #1929`) to say five groups, that `tools arena` and `tools gate` run the AI-game modules apart (#3058), and that `tools, wasm` builds the engine at opt-level 1 and the cards at 0. Also update lines 13–14 of `scripts/ci-scope.sh`, which list the groups `rust_tools_wasm` runs.
- **Estimate**: about 4m per group, against 7m30s now.

**Observation for a person**: `tools duos, selfplay` was not alerted, but `selfplay::` alone takes about 73 s locally on a warm build, plus `duos_fuzz::`, so it may be near or over 5 minutes on CI. I didn't measure which `selfplay::` tests dominate. The new `play_at` seam could cut them, but that is outside this issue's named job.

## Tested (local runs on a 4-core runner, not CI)

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --bin jackioh -- arena:: selfplay_records::` | 20 passed, 1 ignored, finished in 14.89 s (the plan's estimate of the old cost was 92 s + 81 s) |
| `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --bin jackioh -- selfplay::` | 7 passed in 72.7 s, so `play` still works at the full budget |
| `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --bin jackioh -- --skip fuzz:: --skip selfplay:: --skip positions::` | 391 passed, 5 ignored, 32.0 s (the plan measured 181 s before) |
| `cargo fmt --check` | clean |
| `cargo clippy -p jackioh-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |
| `cargo jackioh spec check` | ok: 1697 rulings, 4144 proofs |
| `cargo jackioh catalog check`, `cargo jackioh patches check` | ok |
| `cargo jackioh classify --base 4e0b3b0167 --claims` | `Internal` |

I did not run the full workspace tests, the web tests or the e2e specs. Those are the harness's and CI's checks. The only change outside tests is the `play_chunks` wrapper, which keeps `AI_GATE_BUDGET`.

## Decisions the issue did not settle

- **Lower the budget, not move the tests to `super.yml`.** The rules these tests prove (R850000, R747000, R1676000) are per-pull-request rules, and no cheaper test holds them. A node budget has no clock in it, so determinism and replay hold at any budget.
- **Share one export in `selfplay_records` instead of playing 1 and 2 games separately.** It saves one full export of the same game. The alternative was a second `play_at` call per test.
- **Rejected: `stats.rs`'s `FEW` budget.** At 60 nodes `selfplay_records` had about 25 fallbacks per seat, and its tests assert that no game has faults or fallbacks (R1489000).
- **Rejected: opt-level 2 for `jackioh-ai`.** `Cargo.toml`'s comment already measured it as a loss.

## Look twice

- **`TEST_BUDGET.nodes` is a threshold.** `selfplay_records` needs games with zero fallbacks. I didn't re-measure the threshold: the plan's own runs found 60 nodes fails, 80 passes, and 150 passes with margin. A later AI or engine change could push a decision past it. The fix then is to raise `nodes`, not to drop the fault assertion.
- **Shared `OnceLock`.** If `get_or_init` panics, the cell stays unset and the other test retries, so a failure isn't hidden.

The bot's part was built exactly as the plan said, with no departures.
